title: Beyond the call: Lowe’s Community Impact Grants lift up first responders
summary: Beyond the call: Lowe’s Community Impact Grants lift up first responders
body_markdown:
In Wilkesboro, North Carolina, Fire Chief Jason Smithey knows just how much time firefighters spend at the station.


“We’re here 24 hours a day, so this is a second home


to


our folks,” Smithey said. “We try to keep it as nice and as comfortable as possible.”


The Wilkesboro Fire Department cares for a close-knit community of about 3,800 residents, along with the businesses and industries that keep the town bustling day after day.


But the needs in Wilkesboro reach far beyond putting out fires. “We do everything, practically,” Smithey said. “If something happens, typically we get called for.”


Calls might mean responding to


structure


fires, rescue situations, or even clearing a fallen tree from the road. No matter the challenge, the department steps in to help or


finds


the right hands for the job.


With support from a Lowe’s Community Impact Grant, the department is giving a fresh look to the spaces firefighters return to after a long call. Updates to the day room, kitchen, and sleeping quarters—new flooring, furniture, mattresses, and blinds help make the station feel a little more like home.


For Lowe’s store manager Brandon Hill, the project is also an opportunity for local associates to support the community where they work and live.


“The furniture they


had in


here was stuff they kind


of got


donated to them. That was secondhand,” Hill said. “They’re full-time firefighters, so they stay here. To be able to have a revamped space for them to come together as a family here, and us being able to help support that, has been a real big deal.”


That sense of connection runs deep in Wilkesboro, where Lowe’s has long-standing roots.


“Lowe’s has always given back to this community,” Smithey said. “Most everybody here has somebody that either works for Lowe’s or has worked for Lowe’s in the past. And


so


it’s great to see them come back and help the community.”
